cases.exposure_context_quote: A 45-year-old female presented to a healthcare center after allegedly ingesting 10 mL of 20% PQ, following a familial dispute.
cases.circumstance: ingestion following a familial dispute, with suicidal intent noted in the discussion ('who allegedly ingested PQ with suicidal intent')

symptoms.finding: multiple episodes of projectile vomiting, dizziness, generalized body aches
symptoms.quote: She experienced multiple episodes of projectile vomiting, along with dizziness, and generalized body aches.

symptoms.finding: jaundice, shortness of breath, multiple ulcers over dorsum of tongue ('paraquat tongue') on Day 2
symptoms.quote: She was icteric (Fig. 1), developed shortness of breath, and had multiple ulcers over the dorsum of the tongue, characteristic of a “paraquat tongue” (Fig. 2).
Our patient had now developed acute kidney injury and hepatitis.
Chest radiograph revealed findings of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS).

cases.time_to_care: UNVERIFIED (gastric lavage with activated charcoal performed before referral)

labs.name: renal and liver function tests
labs.value: initially within normal limits; drastic elevations in serum urea, creatinine, bilirubin, AST, and ALT on Day 2
labs.quote: Laboratory test results of RFT and LFT reports revealed drastic elevations in the serum urea, creatinine, bilirubin, aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels (Tables 1 and 2).

labs.name: SOFA score
labs.quote: The patient’s Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score was 8, indicating multiorgan dysfunction.

treatment.name: gastric lavage with activated charcoal
treatment.quote: Gastric lavage with activated charcoal was performed, and she was subsequently referred to our center for further management.

treatment.name: intravenous methylprednisolone (125 mg in 100 mL normal saline followed by 40 mg thrice daily)
treatment.quote: The patient underwent continued gastric lavage along with intravenous methylprednisolone (125 mg in 100 mL normal saline followed by 40 mg thrice daily).

treatment.name: intravenous cyclophosphamide (2 g in 100 mL normal saline)
treatment.quote: she was administered intravenous cyclophosphamide (2 g in 100 mL normal saline)

treatment.name: N-acetyl-cysteine (3.5 gm in 500 mL of 5% dextrose)
treatment.quote: N-acetyl-cysteine (3.5 gm in 500 mL of 5% dextrose)

treatment.name: sylimarin, choline salicylate gel, mesna
treatment.quote: sylimarin tablets were prescribed for hepatoprotection, choline salicylate gel was topically applied for mucosal ulcers and mesna tablets were given to prevent serious side effects of cyclophosphamide.

cases.icu_admission: yes (admitted to the Intensive Care Unit)
cases.outcome: died of progressive multiorgan failure on the fourth day of hospital admission
cases.outcome_quote: Unfortunately, progressive multiorgan failure ensued, and the patient succumbed to her condition on the fourth day of hospital admission.
cases.notes: Supplemental oxygen strictly avoided; baseline chest X-ray and labs within normal limits.
